goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to translate physical accumulation into sampled trapezoidal geometry, MATLAB trapz with explicit coordinates, refinement evidence, analytic-reference validation, simple error, and physical interpretation.

deck_context.deck_context: Week 07 uses one familiar exponentially decaying force model so the new cognitive load is numerical integration. The visible reasoning chain is physical quantity and limits, units, sampled curve, one trapezoid, composite rule, pseudocode, MATLAB trapz, refinement, independent reference, error, validation, and physical interpretation.
deck_context.core_claim: A numerical integral is a physical accumulated area whose unit combines the vertical and horizontal axes. A computed value becomes credible only after its coordinates, units, refinement behaviour, independent reference, and physical meaning have been checked.
deck_context.locked_model: F(t) = F0*exp(-t/tau), F0 = 12 N, tau = 0.8 s, 0 <= t <= T = 2.0 s. Impulse J = integral_0^T F(t) dt has unit N s = kg m/s. Core interval counts are 4, 8, and 16 with spacings 0.500, 0.250, and 0.125 s.
deck_context.locked_evidence: J_exact = 8.8119840132 N s. Trapezoidal estimates for 4, 8, and 16 intervals are 9.0969821492, 8.8835796745, and 8.8299047499 N s. Finest absolute error is 0.0179207367 N s and finest relative error is 0.203368%. The physical bound is 0 < J < 24 N s. The supplied eight-interval Simpson result is 8.8124455163 N s with absolute error about 0.0004615030 N s.
deck_context.exactness: Equations, MATLAB code, variable names, array indices, endpoint weights, limits, sample counts, values, signs, units, axes, validation statements, and numerical evidence are strict teaching content. Do not invent, paraphrase, omit, or approximate them.

style.name: PHY4605 Teaching Courseware - Muted Academic Blue + Sage
style.visual_direction: Clear modern educational slide system matching the approved Week 07 sample and recent Week 03-04 decks, with strong hierarchy, approachable scientific diagrams, and moderate information density.
style.color_palette: Warm-white canvas with deep navy reserved for titles and structural lines. Use a balanced accent family across the deck: dusty blue, teal, clear yellow, warm ochre, coral, warm orange, and restrained red. Green may indicate validation, but red/coral may also distinguish comparison cases or important cautions, while yellow/ochre may highlight concepts, quantities, accumulated areas, or reference values. Avoid making blue and green dominate every slide.
style.typography: Large bold navy sans-serif title aligned flush left; projection-readable body copy; readable monospaced MATLAB code; exact mathematical symbols and units.
style.title_treatment: Every content slide uses a large left-aligned navy title near the upper-left margin and one thin deep-navy horizontal separator immediately below it, extending nearly across the full slide width. Content starts clearly below the rule.
style.density_rule: One dominant learning object, concise supporting copy, and visible whitespace. Split graph, code, and validation into clearly aligned zones.
style.texture_and_finish: Flat clean educational finish, pale fills, thin functional lines, direct labels, no gradients, no decorative clutter, and no thick outer frame.
style.deck_consistency: Match the approved Slide 06 sample's title scale, left alignment, separator line, spacing rhythm, panel treatment, and approachable scientific tone. Preserve navy structure while deliberately rotating blue, teal, yellow, ochre, coral, orange, and red accents by slide role so the deck is coherent but not monotonously blue-green.

slides.title: Pseudocode Before MATLAB
slides.intent: Make the full reasoning algorithm visible before compact MATLAB syntax.
key_points: State quantity, limits, and expected unit.
Choose resolution and create sample coordinates.
Evaluate the model, form trapezoid areas, and add them.
Refine, compare with a reference, then interpret.
slides.local_context: Show a loop from comparison back to resolution. Ask: Which quantities stay fixed during refinement? Fixed: F0, tau, T, model, limits, and units; only interval count/sample spacing changes.
